# AI Assisted Development Control Plane Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `completed`
- Updated: `2026-10-21T02:09:44Z`

## Objective

Deliver a discoverable, portable development control plane that connects user outcomes to scoped AI-assisted work, candidate-bound verification and independent review, realistic evaluations, measured efficiency, safe recovery, and regression feedback through AGENTS.md.

## Discovery

The existing roadmap engine provides durable planning, fingerprinted scope approval, security acceptance, feedback reconciliation, and deterministic rendering. Bounded contributor helpers already own command execution. Completion evidence is currently declarative and lacks candidate-bound execution receipts, mandatory independent technical dispositions, revision-safe coordinated publication, executable coding-agent evaluations, and integrated outcome or efficiency measurement. The comparative review found useful candidate, receipt, review, recovery, and coordination mechanisms in a separate repository, plus coverage and identity limits that should not be reproduced. No existing roadmap owns this contributor control-plane revision. The requested work remains on rebuild.

### Security impact

- Disposition: `security-relevant`
- Summary: Contributor tooling will influence local process execution, implementation scope, evidence freshness, review authority, persistent coordination, and AI evaluation data. Planning records remain inert and grant no execution or external authority.
- Protected assets:
  - Repository source and policy integrity
  - User-authorized scope and approval truth
  - Verification and review evidence
  - Local work ownership and recovery state
  - Protected inputs, model metadata, and sanitized diagnostic output
- Trust boundaries:
  - User authority to agent workflow and lifecycle transitions
  - Tracked policy and approved scope to bounded local command execution
  - Candidate source and test changes to trusted verification and acceptance evidence
  - Separate work or review invocations to immutable candidate-bound dispositions
  - Concurrent local processes to persistent state and generated projections
  - External evaluation results or feedback to deterministic admission and grading
- Abuse and failure cases:
  - A supplied passed status or reviewer label is treated as verified independent evidence
  - A stale receipt or changed check catalog authorizes a different candidate
  - A mixed classified and unclassified change escapes required verification
  - Arbitrary commands, symlinks, traversal, renames, or deletions escape declared scope
  - A concurrent or interrupted write loses work or publishes inconsistent lifecycle state
  - Unbounded execution, output, retries, or model use exhausts resources
  - Private prompts, credentials, raw logs, or personal identifiers leak into tracked records
  - A legacy or rollback path bypasses newly required verification
- Controls:
  - Strict versioned schemas, exact scope and candidate digests, and current check-catalog binding
  - Fixed command identities, preflight plans, contained paths, bounded execution and sanitized receipts
  - Explicit per-path impact accounting and fail-closed missing evidence
  - Candidate-bound review findings, closure evidence, and transparent provenance and identity limits
  - Revision-checked publication, locking, recoverable journals, scoped claims, and explicit recovery
  - Privacy-minimized measurements with unknown values preserved and safety separated from efficiency scores
  - Legacy evidence remains visibly unverified and secure rollback preserves evidence and denial behavior
- Verification:
  - Focused positive and denial tests for stale, forged, incomplete, mismatched, and out-of-scope evidence
  - Traversal, symlink, deletion, rename, timeout, output-bound, and redaction tests
  - Concurrent-writer and interrupted-publication recovery tests on supported local platforms
  - End-to-end contributor fixture covering outcome definition, ownership, verification, independent review, correction, and completion
  - Real evaluation fixtures with repeated-trial accounting, protected grader checks, and explicit unavailable live evidence
  - Documentation and agent-support checks after relevant changes; applicable dependency gate and test:all once at overall completion
- Residual risks:
  - Local digests and append-only conventions do not protect against a malicious actor with unrestricted filesystem or process access
  - Cryptographically authenticated reviewer identity and managed execution hosts need explicit integration decisions and controlled-environment qualification
  - Provider-backed coding-agent performance cannot be claimed from deterministic fixtures or imported unqualified records
  - Platform sandbox and process-tree behavior require real operating-system evidence before stronger isolation guarantees

### Constraints

- Keep AGENTS.md short and make it route every applicable future coding task to one canonical control-plane guide and bounded CLI.
- Preserve existing accepted architecture, product behavior, supported hosts, repository gates, and unrelated work.
- Cover all seven improvement areas from the review; use the fewest economically cohesive increments after the integration decision is approved.
- Keep the roadmap state engine declarative and place generic execution, recovery, and verification in contributor infrastructure.
- Classify every changed path, including deletions and both sides of renames; require fresh evidence for substantive candidate or check-policy changes.
- Support local tree snapshots during iteration and an exact final candidate without forcing commits or granting integration, network, credential, publication, or production authority.
- Preserve legacy roadmap readability and history; never silently promote legacy declarations into verified receipts.
- Use independent review provenance with an explicit cooperative-local trust boundary; labels and hashes alone cannot authenticate an independent actor or resist a malicious local administrator.
- Provide actual fixture execution and grading for agent evaluations; distinguish replay, deterministic conformance, externally supplied live runs, and unavailable live evidence.
- Live model/provider use, confidential input egress, substantial spend, remote mutations, and authenticated host integrations require explicit existing authority and configured adapters.
- Reserve aggregate standard, end-to-end, and AI suite execution for overall completion; run focused change-relevant evidence while increments remain.
- After option approval, define and present the full roadmap with acceptance, rollback, security evidence, and exclusions; implementation begins only after that roadmap is approved.

## High-level decisions

### Development control-plane integration

Should the revised control plane extend the existing roadmap workflow or replace it with a standalone contributor workflow?

Both options cover the seven requested improvements and use AGENTS.md as the entry point. The choice determines durable lifecycle ownership, compatibility, migration work, and how future agents discover and execute repository work. Existing implementation authorization does not settle this new architecture choice or approve an unwritten roadmap.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `integrated-evolution`

AGENTS.md routes future work through that guide. Preserve legacy history with explicit evidence qualification. | yes | Preserves current contribution habits, approved work, and portable skills; Requires coordinated changes to the existing roadmap engine, helper seams, routing, tests, and standards; Adds local integrity controls while documenting the cooperative-local review and execution trust boundary | One canonical workflow and one discovery entry point; No migration to a second capability/slice/packet hierarchy; All seven improvements land as a small number of cohesive, independently qualified increments; Live-agent trials and authenticated review integrations remain explicit adapter boundaries with honest unavailable evidence |

## Increment 1: Outcome-driven delivery with verified completion and safe recovery

- Id: `verified-outcome-delivery`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: None

Give contributors one usable path from AGENTS.md through scoped work and user outcomes to candidate-bound verification, independent technical review, correction, recovery, and honest completion, while preserving the existing roadmap authority and supporting lightweight tasks.

### Work packages

- **Canonical entry point and outcome contracts** (`entry-and-outcomes`): AGENTS.md routes future work to one canonical development-control-plane guide and bounded CLI. A lightweight path handles established local fixes; substantial work uses the existing approved roadmap workflow. Versioned work specifications identify the user or operator problem, critical journey, observable success, relevant baseline, quality constraints, scope, acceptance evidence, and explicit internal-only rationale when applicable.
- **Adapt proven local integrity and coordination mechanisms** (`reuse-and-coordination`): Reuse suitable project-neutral contracts, path confinement, locking, revision checks, transaction recovery, receipt, review, provenance, and lease mechanisms and focused tests from the comparison repository through ai-system-builder-owned adapters. Preserve required provenance and license notices. Scoped claims, revision-safe roadmap publication, bounded renewal, explicit recovery, and actionable status prevent silent overwrite and split lifecycle authority.
- **Bounded candidate verification and execution receipts** (`executed-verification`): A tracked check catalog selects required checks for every changed path. A separate bounded runner emits privacy-minimized receipts tied to source inputs, frozen acceptance, current verification policy, environment, executed check IDs, artifacts, failures, and timeouts. The declarative roadmap engine consumes evidence without becoming a shell runner.
- **Independent review, corrections, and compatibility** (`review-and-completion`): Candidate-bound review records preserve findings and explicit closure evidence, distinguish non-blocking cleanup, reject stale or self-reviewed qualifying submissions, and require fresh evidence after substantive corrections. New governed work cannot complete using unsupported passed declarations. Legacy history remains readable and is explicitly distinguished from receipt-backed qualification.
- **Dynamic local review site** (`dynamic-json-review-site`): A loopback-only read-only review server presents current roadmaps, work, verification, review, evaluations, metrics and feedback from versioned JSON records through a bounded JSON API. AGENTS.md requires starting or safely reusing the server and providing its link for every workflow work request.

### Deliverables

- One documented development control-plane CLI under dev-tools/helpers/ with a cohesive supporting library, stable JSON results, preflight plans, and a read-only status path
- Versioned outcome, work-scope, claim, candidate, check-plan, execution-receipt, review, and completion contracts with local state confined to documented ignored locations
- A reuse inventory identifying the comparison source revision, copied or adapted elements, carried-forward tests, required notices, intentionally omitted coupling, and ai-system-builder-specific corrections
- A tracked check catalog and bounded execution adapter covering existing relevant repository checks and focused tests without arbitrary command arguments from work specifications
- Revision-safe, recoverable state and projection publication integrated with existing roadmap state, plus scoped ownership and explicit lease recovery
- Current architecture and security design documentation, an accepted ADR recording the approved contributor integration boundary, and a focused contributor-control-plane threat model
- Updated AGENTS.md, root and documentation entry points, the roadmap skill and references, helper documentation, evaluation standard, relevant context routing, and cross-agent installation guidance
- Focused Python and Node regression coverage wired into the existing repository test and agent-support paths, including an end-to-end contributor workflow fixture
- A buildless accessible dynamic review site with a documented versioned JSON projection, bounded read-only API, loopback and Host/Origin enforcement, inert rendering, live refresh, and a fixed safe start/status/stop lifecycle.

### Verification

- While implementing, run the focused helper/control-plane Python tests and nearest roadmap, contributor-helper, routing, and policy regression tests for each coherent chunk only.
- After all increment chunks are implemented, run the complete change-relevant control-plane tests, existing roadmap regression tests, focused contributor-helper and agent-support guard tests, and the isolated CLI workflow covering verification, review, correction, completion, and recovery.
- Run npm run docs:check and npm run agent-support:check for the changed guidance and routing, and git diff --check. Run npm run security:dependencies if dependency, build, workflow, or related supply-chain inputs change.
- Exercise candidate and policy drift, mixed uncovered paths, deletion and rename scope, malformed receipts, self-review, blocking findings, expired owners, competing writers, interrupted publication, timeout/output bounds, unsafe paths, and synthetic sensitive-output non-disclosure.
- Audit reuse provenance, license notice retention, absence of source-repository vocabulary in generic mechanisms, and lack of arbitrary shell or external authority in the CLI.
- Reserve npm run test:all and applicable repository-wide completion gates until both roadmap increments are implemented.
- Run focused JSON projection, HTTP security, server lifecycle, UI behavior and live-refresh browser checks for the dynamic review site; verify that no Markdown parser is used as a data source.

### Rollback

Stop admitting new governed work and leave incomplete work visibly unqualified. Preserve existing roadmap state, approvals, source snapshots, claims, receipts, reviews, and recovery journals. Revert the additive integration only after preserving evidence and updating canonical routing; never reinterpret old declarations as current verification, bypass an unresolved ownership conflict, remove user work, or restore a weaker completion policy.

### Excluded

- A second capability/slice/work-packet planning hierarchy or replacement of accepted product architecture
- Automatic Git commits, history rewriting, branch switching, pushes, merges, publication, production mutation, or destructive cleanup
- An unrestricted shell runner, automatic dependency installation, new credentials, automatic network or provider enablement, or expanded host permissions
- A publicly hosted portfolio dashboard, remote-worker scheduler, cross-repository service, or organization identity platform
- Claims that local labels, invocation metadata, append-only files, or hashes defeat an actor with unrestricted local filesystem and process access; authenticated remote review and managed isolation remain successor integrations requiring separate authority and qualification
- Silent product relicensing or copying project-specific source solely to avoid implementing the required ai-system-builder adapter

## Increment 2: Realistic agent evaluations, measured efficiency, and regression feedback

- Id: `evaluated-efficient-development`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `verified-outcome-delivery`

Make the revised control plane useful for improving AI-assisted software delivery by executing and grading realistic repository task trials, comparing quality-adjusted results, measuring bounded run efficiency, and turning meaningful user or operator feedback into durable regression evidence.

### Work packages

- **Prepared coding tasks and executable acceptance grading** (`real-task-evaluations`): Versioned repository-relevant tasks cover a defect, a cross-boundary change, a user-facing journey, a security denial, and a correct decision-gate escalation. The harness prepares isolated work areas and executes fixed trusted graders against resulting artifacts, records actual outcomes and permitted behavior, and keeps repeated trial and environment identity comparable.
- **Privacy-preserving run manifests and quality-adjusted comparisons** (`run-economics`): The control plane records model and harness versions, instruction/context digests, duration, retries, relevant check timing, review corrections, tokens and cost when available, and approved resource limits. Reports compare time and cost per accepted qualified task, preserve missing values as unknown, and prevent efficiency scores from offsetting safety or correctness failure.
- **Feedback, quality qualification, and reusable failure scenarios** (`feedback-regression-loop`): A bounded feedback record links a defect or usability finding to the affected outcome, candidate, acceptance criterion, and regression test or evaluation case. Existing performance and accessibility qualification can be referenced where relevant, and comparison reports distinguish measured improvement, regression, insufficient evidence, and changes requiring a product decision.
- **Public workflow qualification and final handoff** (`integrated-qualification`): One documented public CLI supports prepared agent trials, grading, run accounting, comparison, and feedback closure through the same discovery and authority model as delivery. Combined fixtures exercise the complete revised control plane, and final repository checks establish the implementation's verified boundary and any unavailable external evidence.

### Deliverables

- An executable coding-agent evaluation harness and versioned realistic tasks under dev-tools/agent-evals/, integrated with the existing contributor CLI through bounded operations
- Prepared-trial manifests, protected acceptance inputs, trusted graders, repeatable run accounting, and isolated fixture execution with separately identified deterministic, replay, operator-hosted live, and unavailable evidence
- Versioned privacy-minimized run manifests and comparison reports covering quality, safety, efficiency, retries, rework, environment failures, and comparability limits
- Bounded feedback-to-regression records and quality-evidence references integrated with work status and completion without automatically reprioritizing product scope
- Updated agent-evaluation standards, control-plane guide and CLI examples, AGENTS.md discovery checks, context routing, helper and skill documentation, and applicable provenance notices
- Focused negative and end-to-end tests for real grading, grader integrity, incomparable runs, unknown measurements, unsafe imported results, feedback closure, and protection against rewarding unsafe task completion
- A final concise temporary report with commands, actual outcomes, security disposition, residual risk, and honest distinction between implemented harness capability and externally measured coding-agent performance

### Verification

- During internal chunks, run only focused evaluation, run-manifest, metric-comparison, feedback, CLI, and nearest routing/skill tests.
- After all increment chunks are implemented, run its change-relevant tests and public CLI fixtures, including actual failing and passing task outputs, correct abstention/escalation, grader substitution, repeated trials, unavailable measurements, incomparable runs, and feedback-to-regression closure.
- Run npm run docs:check, npm run agent-support:check, and git diff --check after affected guidance and context changes.
- At the overall boundary after both increments are implemented, run npm run test:all once, npm run docs:check, npm run agent-support:check, npm run architecture:check, and npm run security:dependencies when supply-chain inputs changed. Run additional builds only when the implementation affects their wiring.
- Validate the roadmap state and generated artifacts; audit the AGENTS.md discovery path and all seven requested improvement areas against actual delivered evidence.
- Record any missing live-provider, authenticated-review-host, dedicated performance, or platform-specific isolation evidence as outside the qualified local boundary rather than as a successful result.

### Rollback

Disable new evaluation-trial or feedback admission while preserving trial manifests, source references, grading receipts, metric reports, feedback links, and the verified delivery workflow from increment 1. Revert only additive evaluation and measurement behavior after updating routing and standards. Never fabricate a baseline, convert unknown cost to zero, erase a failed trial, weaken the independent grader, or discard regression evidence to make a comparison pass.

### Excluded

- Automatic provider/model enablement, credential collection, confidential input egress, substantial spend, or remote agent execution without existing explicit operator authority
- A model leaderboard, promises of coding-agent superiority, or claiming live performance without qualified actual trials
- Automatic production analytics collection, user tracking, public telemetry export, or product reprioritization from feedback
- Model training, production application feature changes, unrelated UI redesign, or replacement of existing product performance and accessibility qualification
- Claims of authenticated reviewer identity or hostile-code isolation that require a future approved host integration and controlled qualification
